vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: apiclaw-analysis
Version: 1.1.5

The apiclaw-analysis skill bundle is a legitimate tool for Amazon product research, providing an interface to the APIClaw service. The core logic is contained in a Python script (scripts/apiclaw.py) that uses only standard libraries to communicate with the official API endpoint (api.apiclaw.io). The skill instructions (SKILL.md) and reference documents provide detailed guidance for the AI agent to perform market analysis, risk assessment, and listing optimization without any evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection. Credential handling is limited to the APICLAW_API_KEY, which is stored locally in an environment variable or a configuration file.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are consistent with an Amazon research API client; the only notable issues are that it persists the API key to a local config file and asks the agent to execute a bundled script, which are functional choices but have privacy implications you should consider.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Amazon product research) match what the files implement: a CLI wrapper that calls api.apiclaw.io endpoints. The single declared credential (APICLAW_API_KEY) is exactly what this API client needs; no unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to execute scripts/apiclaw.py for all API calls, to run specific query flows (e.g., automatic 'product --asin' supplements), and to include API usage metadata in outputs. Those instructions stay within the stated purpose, but they explicitly direct the agent to write the user-provided API key into a local config.json file and to run the provided script rather than loading responses from elsewhere — both are behavioral choices the user should be aware of (they grant file write and script-execution activity in the skill directory).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only plus a bundled script. That minimizes supply-chain risk (no external downloads). The script is included in the skill bundle and uses only standard Python stdlib (urllib), so there are no surprising package installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one secret (APICLAW_API_KEY) is required and it matches the described API usage. However, the skill and SKILL.md instruct that when the user provides a key it will be saved to config.json in the skill directory (fallback to env var preferred). Persisting an API key unencrypted to disk increases risk of accidental exposure (workspace backups, shared machines, commits) even though the repo claims config.json is .gitignored.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not ask for system-wide config changes. It will read and potentially write a config.json in its own skill directory to persist the API key — a local persistence behavior that is coherent with its purpose but is a privilege (file write) the user should accept consciously. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but not elevated by the skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (a client for api.apiclaw.io). Before installing: 1) Prefer providing the key via the APICLAW_API_KEY environment variable rather than typing it into the agent UI, because SKILL.md says the skill will save any provided key to a plaintext config.json in the skill folder. 2) Be aware the agent will execute the bundled Python script (scripts/apiclaw.py) and that script will make HTTPS POSTs only to api.apiclaw.io (no other endpoints were found), but review the script yourself if you want assurance. 3) Avoid storing the API key in shared or versioned workspaces; rotate the key if it may have been exposed. 4) If you need stronger protection, use an ephemeral or restricted API key and run the skill in an isolated agent/workspace.
